record.paper_title: Twenty open problems in quantum control
record.original_question: For open-loop quantum control, where the task is to vary a Hamiltonian H = sum_n c_n H_n in time to obtain a desired evolution, which control objectives and which available sets of control Hamiltonians H_n make the control problem easy, with the time-dependent-control complexity scaling polynomially in the logarithm of the system size? Does the class of easy objectives depend nontrivially on the chosen set of available Hamiltonians?

evidence.quote: Usually one is faced with a Hamiltonian of the form H = ∑ n cnHn, where the classical parameters cn can be varied with time in a more-or-less arbitrary way.
A problem is easy if the complexity of the time-dependent control scales as a polynomial in the logarithm of the size of the system

Problem 18: For what control objectives, and what set of control Hamiltonians, is open-loop control easy? Does the set of easy objectives depend in a non-trivial way on the set of control Hamiltonians?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an open-loop quantum control setting in which a quantum system of Hilbert-space dimension N evolves under a time-dependent Hamiltonian of the form
   H(t) = Σ_n c_n(t) H_n,
where {H_n} is a fixed finite set of Hermitian "control Hamiltonians" available to the experimenter, and the real-valued coefficients c_n: [0,T] → ℝ are classical control functions that may be varied essentially arbitrarily in time. A control objective is a specification of a desired property of the resulting unitary evolution U(T) = T-exp(−i ∫₀ᵀ H(t) dt) (for example, implementing a target unitary up to a prescribed accuracy, or steering an initial state to a target state).

Define the "time-dependent-control complexity" of an objective, given a control set {H_n}, to be the minimum description complexity (e.g., piecewise-constant pulse count plus bit-precision, or any equivalent reasonable measure) of a control schedule {c_n(t)} that achieves the objective. Call the control problem "easy" for a given pair (objective, {H_n}) if this complexity scales polynomially in log N as N → ∞.

Characterize, as completely as possible, the pairs (control objective, set of available control Hamiltonians {H_n}) for which the open-loop control problem is easy in the above sense. In particular, determine whether the class of "easy" objectives depends nontrivially on the choice of the available set {H_n}: i.e., do there exist objectives that are easy for some admissible control sets but provably not easy for others?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as Problem 18 in a 2013 list of twenty open problems in quantum control. A general characterization of "easy" open-loop control objectives in terms of polylog(N) control complexity remains an active research topic (related to quantum compiling, Solovay–Kitaev-type results, and quantum speed limits), but no comprehensive answer has been established in the literature, and no source claims a resolution of this specific question.
